summary: Extended the simultaneous-restart harness with the remediation that matters for the headline progress loss and verified it locally: after the flagged restart leaves all three voters with empty configurations and no leader, stopping those same three nodes and restarting them on the same durable stores with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled brings all three back with the configuration and elects a leader within eight seconds (servers [3,3,3], nodes_with_full_config 3, leader at index 2), while the control mode's phases are unchanged. That makes the impact bound concrete: the loss is in-memory and reversible by an ordinary restart without discarding any durable state, so the state is recoverable as soon as an operator notices it — while nothing in-protocol can repair it, which is what made the cluster unavailable in the first place. The revision is submitted as a successor of the current cluster-wide experiment with the earlier comparisons preserved and two added (all voters configured again; a leader electable again), and the interpretation records the remediation as pending that receipt.
